liam_delta: Hey team — since 22:00 UTC we've been seeing a sharp spike in 429s and p99 latency on /v1/generate for the delta-prod pool. Impacting customers in EU region.
anya_support: Sorry you're hitting this, liam. Can you share baseline QPS, the peak you saw, and whether you were on Dedicated pool or Hosted? :wave:
liam_delta: We're on Dedicated (delta-prod). Baseline steady QPS around 18, then flash spike to ~220 sustained ~7m, then multiple 60-90s tails. Token sizes averaged 900-1.2k.
anya_support: Thanks — that's helpful. Can you paste the autoscale config/limits for the pool (min/max replicas, target utilization) or confirm if you have any hard throttles configured?
liam_delta: Here is the pool config our infra console shows:
```
pool: delta-prod
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 10
target_gpu_util: 0.65
burst_headroom_tokens: 0
queue_threshold_ms: 500
route_rate_limit: none
```
liam_delta: We didn't enable burst headroom because we thought the max 10 replicas would be fine.
anya_support: Copy that. Curious — were any other large jobs running in the same capacity? Asking because noisy neighbor could explain persistent tails even after replicas scale. Any long-running streaming or embedding jobs around same time?
jordan_sre: I pulled metrics from the cluster — looks like autoscaler did react but the scale-up lag was ~45s to add replicas, and p95 spiked before new pods came online. Also GPU utilization per-host was uneven: a couple of instances at 98% and others idle. Might be scheduling packing + large KV cache hot-shards.
jordan_sre: Quick snippet of metrics (UTC window 21:50-22:10):
```
baseline_qps: 18
peak_qps: 220 (22:02)
avg_tokens_per_request: 950
p95_latency_before_scale: 1.15s
p95_latency_during_peak: 3.9s
scale_up_time: 45s
replicas_before: 3
replicas_after: 9
avg_gpu_util_post_scale: 72% (but skewed)
queue_length_peak: 42
```
kyle_eng: From infra side, two observations: (1) min_replicas=2 is too low for sudden bursts of that magnitude — you want enough baseline headroom to absorb short spikes while scale-up completes; (2) queue_threshold_ms 500ms means requests sit queued instead of allowing early tail shedding. Consider lowering queue_threshold or enabling burst_headroom_tokens so we can provision transient capacity without hitting max_replicas.
liam_delta: OK — what's a recommended baseline for our traffic profile? We don't want to pay for idle GPUs but also not break during campaigns.
anya_support: Quick heuristic — set min_replicas to cover ~2x baseline QPS at p95 token cost. For you that'd be ~40 QPS = ~4-5 replicas depending on GPU model. Then enable burst_headroom_tokens ~50-100 to handle 5-10s surges, and raise max_replicas to 14 if you expect large campaigns. Also set a route-level rate_limit for unauthenticated or noisy clients.
jordan_sre: Also advise per-route token limit (e.g., max_tokens 2k) and short-circuit for very long generations. That reduces KV pressure and average token work. For noisy neighbor detection: set alerts on skewed host GPU util and per-host p99 latency — if one host is at 95%+ while others are low, it's a scheduling hotspot.
liam_delta: Do you want logs / repro steps? I can provide recent request IDs.
ya_support: Please do — request IDs + approximate times help us map to infra traces. Also run this on your side to give us a compact snapshot: `rwcctl metrics query --pool delta-prod --range 30m --agg p95,p99 --by host,route` and paste the output.
ops-bot: Deployment notice: autoscaler v2 rolled out to eu-region clusters on 2026-01-12 04:00 UTC — features: faster scale-up, burst_headroom toggle.
kyle_eng: If you're comfortable, we can provision a temporary isolated burst pool (delta-burst) for the campaign window. That avoids noisy neighbor and is cheap if used only during bursts. We bill reserved GPUs per-hour but you can enable auto-stop.
liam_delta: I'll try the config changes (min_replicas=5, burst_headroom_tokens=80, max_replicas=14) for the next push and post the command outputs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
anya_support: Great — ping us with the rwcctl output and any request IDs. We'll keep an eye and can open a proactive escalation if autoscale still lags.
liam_delta: Posting rwcctl output now, attaching 3 request IDs: rq_8c4f, rq_8c5a, rq_8d00 (22:02:14-22:04:00 UTC).
anya_support: Got them — we're correlating traces, will update in this thread. :mag_right:
